docs.title: Visiban
docs.text:
Pre-release

1.2.0-alpha.2 is a pre-release development build of the upcoming release — expect bugs and breaking changes. Report issues or see the installation guide if you want to try it early.

A self-hosted Kanban board with swimlane rows and automatic card movement tracking — a lightweight alternative to Trello/Smartsheet with a full audit trail of every card move between columns and swimlanes, focused on pipeline visibility per customer or project.

In one line: kill the spreadsheet, visualize the workflow, interrogate it with your own AI — every move on the record. Rows are entities with typed fields of their own, so the data that used to live in a side-spreadsheet lives on the board. Every card movement is recorded permanently. And a first-class MCP server lets any AI agent you already run query and update the board through a token you issue — Visiban ships the interface, not a model, so nothing leaves your install.

New here, or comparing options? Why Visiban covers what makes it different and, honestly, when to pick something else.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• Swimlanes — rows represent entities (customers, projects, teams); columns are pipeline stages
  • Movement history — every drag logs from/to column, from/to swimlane, who moved it, and when; board-level History tab with search and filters
  • Real-time updates — board state syncs live across all open tabs via WebSocket (Django Channels + Valkey)
  • Analytics — summary view (card counts, velocity) and analytics view (dwell time, bottlenecks, stalled cards)
  • Board sharing — generate a read-only public link; anyone with the URL can view the board without logging in
  • Saved filters — save and restore filter presets per board; private to each user
  • Notifications — assignee alerts on card assignment; @mention alerts; staleness alerts when cards haven't moved in N days
  • Groups — organize boards into groups and sub-groups with inherited membership
  • RBAC — five roles with fine-grained per-board and per-group permissions; moderator entitlement for content moderation
  • OAuth & OIDC — Google, GitHub, and GitLab login out of the box; connect any OIDC provider via environment variables
  • Personal access tokens — token-based API access for scripts and integrations
  • Invite links — shareable URLs with configurable role, expiry, and single-use options
  • Production-ready — Nginx reverse proxy with flexible TLS (letsencrypt, selfsigned, or none) via docker-compose.prod.yml and init-prod.sh

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text:
All notable changes to Visiban are documented here.

The format follows Keep a Changelog and Semantic Versioning.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text: • scripts/release.sh now shows the release notes extracted from CHANGELOG.md's [Unreleased] section — the same text that becomes the dated CHANGELOG entry and the GitLab Release page body — and asks for confirmation before touching any other file, right after creating the release branch. Aborting leaves the tree untouched (git reset --hard, back to main, release branch deleted). Non-interactive runs (used by the /release skill after the user has approved the notes in chat) pass -y/--yes or set RELEASE_ASSUME_YES=1; a non-TTY run without either now fails closed instead of shipping unreviewed notes. Mirrors the release-summary confirmation TruePPM's scripts/release.sh already had.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text: • scripts/release.sh now bumps helm/visiban/Chart.yaml's appVersion on every release, alongside the existing helm/visiban/values.yaml image tag pin. Previously it was never updated, so the helm-publish CI job's appVersion-vs-tag guard failed at tag time and no chart was published for that release — this affected v1.2.0-alpha.1, whose Helm chart was never published; the demo site at try.visiban.com deploys from this chart, so it stayed on the previous release until this fix.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Hosted demo support: opt-in DEMO_MODE shows a live-demo banner with credentials on the login page, and seed_demo_data --demo-site seeds Software, Marketing, and Hiring boards with an admin and two member accounts. Off by default; existing installs are unchanged (#1034). The deployment ships as the Helm chart's public demo mode (#1180).
  • Issue Board Lens outbound-call observability for site admins: every GitHub/GitLab API call the lens makes is now counted (per provider, resource kind and outcome) and written as one structured git_lens.outbound log line with no tokens or query values. The new admin-only GET /api/v1/admin/git-lens/usage/ endpoint reports the last 24 hours of counts, cache hit/miss outcomes, and the fixed limits that bound the traffic. Only available with GIT_LENS_ENABLED=true; log verbosity is set with the new optional GIT_LENS_OUTBOUND_LOG_LEVEL (default INFO) (#1061).
  • The issue board lens's columns and swimlane-label panel are now drag-resizable, mirroring the native board's resize gesture (mouse drag, or arrow keys on a focused resize handle). Sizes are remembered per board in your browser. Row-height resizing is not included in this change (#1065).
  • The Issue Board Lens filter row gains label and assignee filters, and an explicit (no milestone) option in the milestone control. Like the existing state and milestone filters, both new filters are applied at the provider rather than in the browser, so they reach issues that fall outside the 300-issue fetch cap — filtering to a label is now a way to see more work, not less. Labels combine with "and" (an issue must carry every selected label) and up to five can be selected at once. GitHub milestone filtering also moved server-side: it previously ran in the browser over the already-fetched page, which silently dropped matching issues beyond the cap (#1067).
  • The issue board lens now highlights the current milestone when swimlaning by milestone — it sorts to the top of the board and is marked with a "Current" badge, so what's actively being worked on stands out instead of being buried among all milestones. The current milestone is detected automatically (nearest active milestone by due date, falling back to the one with the most in-progress work), with no setup.
  • Added backend-diff-coverage and frontend-diff-coverage, MR-only CI jobs that measure test coverage of only the lines an MR changes (via diff-cover, reusing the existing coverage.xml / cobertura-coverage.xml reports — no test re-run), blocking at 80% of changed lines. The existing aggregate coverage gates (backend-test-coverage's 90%, the frontend's vitest thresholds) measure the whole codebase and can absorb a fully untested new feature without moving the total; these new jobs close that gap and print the uncovered line numbers directly in the job log (#1076).
  • Added a ws-event-reachability CI gate that reconciles every WebSocket event name across the three places it lives — emitted, documented, and handled — so a name present in only two of them can no longer look complete. The emitted set is now declared as a registry in boards/broadcast.py and groups/broadcast.py that every broadcast call site draws from; a bare string literal at an emit site fails the gate. Documented lens_connection.configured, lens_connection.removed, the group channel's member.removed, and invite_link.revoked, which were emitted and handled but missing from the WebSocket API reference. No wire format changed.
  • A serializer-ts-parity CI gate now compares the generated OpenAPI schema against the hand-written TypeScript interfaces in frontend/src/types/index.ts, so a serializer field added, removed, or retyped without its frontend counterpart fails the pipeline instead of drifting silently. It covers Board, Card, User, BoardMembership and BoardUser, checking field presence in both directions plus type family, nullability, and enum membership. Known mismatches are recorded as self-invalidating suppressions that fail the gate once the drift they cite is fixed, so a suppression cannot outlive its reason. See docs/development/serializer-ts-parity.md (#1079).
  • Added backend-schema-fuzz, a CI job that fuzzes the live API against its declared OpenAPI schema with schemathesis, authenticated as a normal board member, to catch responses that don't match what the schema describes (#1080). Non-blocking for this release while its baseline findings are triaged (#1120).
  • Added nightly-load-test, a schedule-only CI job that measures real p50/p95/p99 latency for the board-fetch, card-search (trigram-indexed), card-timeline (activity/movement feed), and notifications-poll endpoints against a large seeded fixture (manage.py seed_demo_data --scale N --with-notifications, ~2,400 cards), and fails the scheduled pipeline if any endpoint exceeds its committed budget. Closes the gap the existing perf-check/perf-bench query-count gates cannot see: a regression from a missing index or a data-volume change can leave the query count identical while making the same queries slower. Budgets are committed in backend/nightly-load-test-baseline.json, derived from a measured baseline (~1.4x, per a documented formula) and re-derived at each release — see docs/development/nightly-load-test.md (#1082).
  • CI gate docs-version-accuracy fails when README.md, VISIBAN_FEATURES.md or docs/ carry a stale "Coming in X" / "Ships in X" / "Planned for X" claim for an already-released version, when a GA version still has the release-candidate banner or stale install pins, or when a tag does not match the version in frontend/package.json. scripts/release.sh now rewrites the docs/index.md banner on GA releases as well as RC.
  • Added a SUPPRESSED-UNTIL(#NNNN) marker convention for temporary suppressions (eslint-disable, pytest.mark.skip/xfail), a suppressions-check CI job (scripts/check-suppression-issues.sh) that queries the GitLab API and fails when a cited marker's issue is already closed, and documentation at docs/development/suppressions.md. Runs on merge requests, main, and scheduled pipelines — not MR-only, since the triggering event is an issue closing rather than a commit landing. Backfilled every previously-unjustified frontend/src eslint-disable with a permanent reason; audited the backend's skip/skipif/xfail sites and found each already carried an adequate reason (environment gating, no marker needed) (#1092).
  • CI gate scripts now follow a --self-test house rule: osv-severity-gate.sh and
  • assemble-changelog.sh gained self-test modes, check-migration-numbering.sh's existing
  • self-test is now actually invoked by its CI job, and a new gate-selftest-parity meta-gate
  • derives the list of bespoke gate scripts from .gitlab-ci.yml itself and fails if any lacks
  • a working, wired self-test. See docs/development/ci-gates.md for the convention, the
  • documented exemptions, and known gaps (#1093).
  • Added a /kaizen skill that audits the development harness itself — it reads the ## Gates ledger CLAUDE.md has required on every MR, computed via a new scripts/kaizen_gate_ledger.py parser, and reports each gate's run count, n/a/skipped/0 findings breakdown, yield, and ledger adoption rate across a window of recently merged MRs. It flags gates with fewer than 10 recorded runs as inconclusive, names concrete fast-path narrowing candidates for gates at 0% yield over 10+ runs (never a deletion — only a narrower trigger), and confirms gates over 50% yield as load-bearing. Distinct from /pre-release, which audits the codebase rather than the harness (#1094).
  • migration-check now fails a migration that adds a constraint, a NOT NULL column, or a
  • unique field to a populated table without a preceding data-repair step — this pattern used
  • to crash-loop at deploy time instead of failing gracefully. Escape hatch: an inline
  • # constraint-safe: <reason> comment (#1098).
  • WebSocket connections can now be authenticated with a short-lived ticket, so clients that authenticate to the REST API with a token — native, CLI, and front ends served from another origin — receive live board and group updates instead of being closed with 4001. Call POST /api/v1/auth/ws-ticket/ with any supported credential and pass the returned value as ?ticket= on the upgrade. Tickets are single-use, expire after 30 seconds, and are stored hashed; they authenticate only, so board and group membership is still enforced on every connection. The browser SPA's session-cookie handshake is unchanged (#1109).
  • Added GET /api/v1/cards/ — a paginated, filterable card query across every board the requesting user can access, for table/list views over large boards and for incremental sync. Supports filtering by board, swimlane, column, assignee, label, priority, due date range, and updated_since, plus text search, with cursor pagination ({results, next_cursor}) so a client can page through thousands of cards or poll for changes without missing or duplicating rows under concurrent writes. The existing GET /api/v1/boards/{board_id}/cards/ (200-row cap, no pagination) and GET /api/v1/boards/{board_id}/full/ (unpaginated) are unchanged (#1112).
  • Board change feed: GET /api/v1/boards/{id}/events/ returns committed board mutations in id order with a resumable after cursor, so a consumer outside the Django process can replay what it missed after a dropped WebSocket instead of re-fetching /full/. Every event the board channel broadcasts is persisted in the same transaction as the mutation it describes, and WebSocket frames now carry an additive event_id naming the matching feed row. Events are retained for BOARD_EVENT_RETENTION_DAYS days (default 30) and removed by the new prune_board_events management command; a cursor that has aged out returns 410 Gone with a re-sync hint rather than a page that silently skips events.
  • Helm chart deploy testing: the chart now ships a values.schema.json (unknown or
  • misspelled values keys are rejected instead of silently doing nothing), a helm test
  • hook so operators can verify an install actually booted, and values-dev.yaml /
  • values-prod.yaml overlays. CI gained kubeconform validation, a deploy-contract
  • gate, a kind boot drill, and a Calico NetworkPolicy enforcement drill; release tags
  • now publish a Cosign-signed chart to oci://ghcr.io/visiban/charts.
  • Admin action log — changes to instance-wide settings are now recorded with who made them and when, readable by site admins from GET /api/v1/admin/action-log/. Covers the maintenance mode toggle and its notice, registration mode, and the file-uploads switch, whether the change was made from the admin panel, the maintenance_mode management command, or the Django admin. Only real transitions are recorded, so the gap between an enabled and a disabled entry is the true length of a maintenance window. Previously the only trace of a flip was the setting's current value, which made "who put the instance into maintenance?" unanswerable during an incident retrospective.
  • Custom fields on swimlane rows (#1140). Board admins can define typed metadata fields that attach to swimlane rows rather than cards — text, number, date, dropdown, and checkbox — managed in Board Settings → Swimlane fields, a new tab beside the existing card fields tab (which is renamed from "Fields" to "Card fields" so the pair reads unambiguously). Rows represent entities such as an account, project, or candidate, and until now everything but name, contact email, and notes had to be stuffed into the notes field as prose. Up to 15 fields per board, of which 3 can be pinned to the swimlane row header; pinned values render as chips in the row's label panel, and a +N chip opens the full list. Values are edited in the Edit Swimlane modal and appear in /full/, the swimlane serializers, CSV and JSON export, and the swimlane.updated WebSocket payload. Filtering and sorting by swimlane field values is not in this release — see the limitations table in the docs. Each field carries an Admin only toggle, on by default, which serves that field's values to board admins alone — members and viewers never receive them, and anonymous share links never receive any row field values at all. A field's type is frozen once any swimlane holds a value for it, enforced server-side rather than only warned about in the UI.
  • Swimlane row field definitions broadcast swimlane_custom_field.created, swimlane_custom_field.updated, swimlane_custom_field.deleted, and swimlane_custom_field.reordered on the board channel, so a second admin's Board Settings stays in step without a reload (#1140).
  • Swimlane updates arriving over the WebSocket are now merged into local board state rather than replacing it wholesale, so an admin no longer loses a row's contact_email and notes from their own screen when another admin edits that swimlane. This was a pre-existing bug that row field values would have made considerably worse (#1140).
  • Added two CI gates, rbac-coverage (scripts/check-rbac-coverage.py) and broadcast-deferral (scripts/check-broadcast-deferral.py), which assert statically what the rbac-check and broadcast-check agent gates previously asserted by reading each diff. rbac-coverage checks that every board/group-scoped endpoint has an authentication gate, resolves the caller's role through the shared resolver rather than a raw membership lookup, applies a minimum-role check on every write action, and scopes board-child lookups so a global pk cannot cross boards. broadcast-deferral checks that every such write reaches a broadcast, that every raw broadcast_*_event() sits inside a transaction.on_commit() callable, that no commit hook holds an ORM row read from the enclosing scope, and that no emit call sits in a loop over rows of one channel. Both run in the test stage with needs: [] in well under a second, both ship a --self-test per the #1093 house rule, and both distinguish "unhandled pattern — hand it to the agent" (exit 3) from a pass, so a view whose authorization cannot be read statically fails the pipeline instead of passing silently. Recorded exceptions live in self-invalidating tables in each script. No application behavior changed. See docs/development/rbac-and-broadcast-gates.md (#1143).
  • Harness: a scheduled kaizen-yield-watch job (scripts/kaizen_yield_watch.py) now keeps a running per-gate, per-diff-shape zero-finding count from the MR ## Gates ledger and reports gates that reach 10 consecutive 0-finding runs, so gate drift no longer waits on a manual /kaizen run. Report-only by default; opt-in issue filing; never edits the fast-path table.
  • Added a generic grid overlay slot to the board view: a pluggable layer that shades each board cell from a per-cell number without changing the grid's layout. An overlay supplies only a value and a label per cell; the slot owns the scale, the tint, the legend, and the empty state — including the accessibility contract, so every step is encoded three ways (tint, the height of a bar on the cell's bottom edge, and the value itself) and no overlay can ship a color-only ramp (#969). Two overlays ship: None (the default — the board renders exactly as before) and Card count, a reference overlay computed from the cards already loaded, adding no queries. Pick one from the Overlay dropdown in the board toolbar; the choice is remembered per board (#1147).
  • Scheduled jobs: the due-date (notify_due_soon) and staleness (notify_stale_cards) notification scans, and the prune_board_events / prune_notifications retention jobs, now have a shipped scheduler. For Docker Compose it is an opt-in scheduler service (profile scheduler, new run_scheduler command, times set by SCHEDULE_* env vars in UTC). For Helm it is native CronJobs under scheduledJobs. Both are off by default, so upgrading changes nothing. Until you enable one of them, or schedule the commands from host cron, users who turn on due-date or staleness notifications receive nothing. Within the scheduler, the notification scans are on and the prune jobs are off until enabled individually. If you already run these commands from host cron, remove those lines before you enable the scheduler, to avoid duplicate notifications. See docs/administration/scheduled-jobs.md.
  • Notification retention: new prune_notifications management command deletes in-app notifications, read or unread, older than NOTIFICATION_RETENTION_DAYS (new env var, default 90 days, minimum 14). It supports --days, --batch-size and --dry-run. It runs only when scheduled, and the shipped scheduler leaves it off, so existing installs keep every notification until an operator enables it. The 14-day floor exists because notification rows are also the de-duplication record for the scheduled notification scans.
  • The Helm chart gains a public demo mode (demo.enabled, off by default, reference values in values-demo.yaml): a self-seeding install, an hourly whole-database reset CronJob whose schedule also drives the visitor countdown (with the reset disabled, the login page no longer promises one), an egress NetworkPolicy limiting demo pods to DNS and their own datastores, render guards against publishing a login on a writable instance, and a helm test that proves the write fence through the frontend (#1180). New NUM_PROXIES setting (Helm backend.settings.numProxies, default 1, unchanged for existing installs) sets how many reverse proxies to trust in X-Forwarded-For, so per-IP throttles see the real client behind a tunnel instead of one shared address.
  • Site admins can now configure outbound email (SMTP) from Admin → Settings → Email instead of environment variables, with a Send test email button that delivers to the admin's own address and reports a specific reason on failure. The SMTP password is encrypted at rest. Existing installs are unaffected: environment variables remain the default source and are used until an admin explicitly switches over, and setting EMAIL_BACKEND explicitly continues to override everything. Adds the EMAIL_USE_SSL and EMAIL_TIMEOUT environment variables, plus an optional VISIBAN_SECRET_ENCRYPTION_KEY for installs that rotate DJANGO_SECRET_KEY. The DEFAULT_FROM_EMAIL placeholder check moved from startup to send time, so a fresh production instance now boots and can be configured entirely through the UI.
  • Cards can now link to a pull request or merge request (GitHub, GitLab, or any other http/https URL). The link appears as a small badge on the card face that opens it in a new tab, and is set, edited, or removed from a new "Pull / merge request" section in the card detail panel — pasting a GitHub PR or GitLab MR URL fills in the provider and reference automatically. It is also available on the REST API as the card's external_ref field ({provider, ref, url}), carried in real-time updates and JSON board export/import, and deliberately left off public share links (#352).
  • Added a Why Visiban page to the documentation — what differentiates Visiban (entity rows with typed fields, movement history as structured data, a bring-your-own-model MCP interface, and SSO in the OSS core) plus an honest side-by-side comparison against Trello, Linear, GitLab/GitHub boards, Monday/ClickUp/Asana, Notion, Vikunja/Plane, Planka, WeKan/Kanboard/Focalboard, and dedicated CRMs — including when to pick one of those instead. Every competitive claim carries the date it was verified.
  • Notifications can now be delivered by email as well as in the app, for four events: a card assigned to you, an @mention in a comment or description, a card due within 24 hours, and a card you own moved to another column. Each event has its own per-user opt-in under Settings → Notifications, and every one of them defaults to off — upgrading an instance that already has SMTP configured does not start emailing anybody, and nothing is sent until a user opts in for themselves. Delivery uses plain SMTP through the existing email configuration (EMAIL_HOST/EMAIL_PORT/EMAIL_USE_TLS/DEFAULT_FROM_EMAIL, or Admin → Settings → Email) with no third-party service; two new variables, NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_ENABLED and NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_TIMEOUT, give operators an instance-wide off switch and a send timeout. A mail failure never breaks the action that caused it. The due-date notification itself is also new — earlier releases documented it and shipped its preference toggle, but nothing created it; it is produced by a new idempotent notify_due_soon management command (#356).
  • Custom fields (#371) now have a full UI. Board admins can define, reorder, and pin up to 2 typed fields to the card face from a new Fields tab in Board Settings — text, number, date, dropdown, or checkbox. Pinned dropdown and checkbox values are editable directly from the card face without opening the card. Every field, pinned or not, is editable from the card detail panel, and the hover peek surfaces any non-pinned values that have data. The filter bar gained a control per pinned field, plus a picker to filter by any other custom field on demand.
  • Custom fields on cards — board admins can now define typed metadata fields per board (text, number, date, dropdown, checkbox), and cards carry values for them. Where a label is an untyped tag, a custom field is a named key with a type: "Array type = raid10", "Hypervisors = 4". Manage the schema at /api/v1/boards/{id}/custom-fields/ (admin only; readable by every board member, viewers included), and read and write a card's values as custom_field_values on the existing card endpoints — the same shape both ways, so the representation the API returns can be sent straight back. Values are validated per type, a cleared field is removed rather than blanked, and up to 30 fields per board can be defined with at most 2 pinned to the card face. Custom fields are included in CSV and JSON board exports (additively — the export schema version is unchanged), arrive with the board on /full/ as custom_field_definitions, and are deliberately excluded from public share links, which stay anonymous. Backend only in this release: the card detail UI, card-face pinning, and filtering by field value follow in 1.2 (#371).
  • Card relations — link cards on the same board as blocks / blocked by or relates to. Blocked cards carry a red indicator on the card face so dependencies are visible while scanning the board, and the card detail panel lists every relation with the linked card and its direction. Archived blockers are excluded from the indicator but stay listed so a dangling link can be removed. Adds blocker_count to the card payload and GET/POST/DELETE endpoints at /boards/{board_id}/cards/{id}/relations/.
  • Import a Trello board JSON export into a new Visiban board. A two-step wizard (reached from Import → Import a Trello export) previews the mapping before anything is created: lists become columns, labels keep their colors and can optionally become swimlanes, checklists, comments (with original timestamps), and archived cards carry over, and attachment links are added to card descriptions. Trello members are matched by username only among people you can already see, and the preview reports just a count of matches. Backed by the new POST /api/v1/boards/import/trello/ endpoint (?dry_run=true / ?confirm=true). The upload limit is configurable with the new VISIBAN_IMPORT_MAX_SIZE setting (bytes, default 25 MB; Helm: backend.settings.importMaxSizeBytes), and the bundled nginx body limit is raised from 20 MB to 35 MB to match (#456).
  • MCP (Model Context Protocol) server — connect Claude, Copilot, or any MCP-compatible AI agent to Visiban and let it read your boards. The server is served at /mcp over the Streamable HTTP transport and authenticates with an existing Personal Access Token sent as Authorization: Bearer <token>. This first release ships one tool, list_boards, which returns every board the token's owner can access along with their effective role and column, swimlane, and card counts. Off by default; operators enable it with MCP_SERVER_ENABLED=true.
  • MCP server: added the full set of OSS CRUD tools for AI agents — list_columns, list_swimlanes, and list_cards (filterable by column, swimlane, assignee, priority, and label) for reading board state, and create_card, move_card, update_card, and archive_card for writing it. Write tools require an admin or member board role and now additionally require the token to carry the mcp:write scope (previously documented as reserved but unenforced, since no write tool existed yet), so an mcp:read-only agent credential stays read-only. Every write reuses the same service functions, WIP/weight enforcement, CardMovement audit trail, and WebSocket broadcast as the REST API — a blocked move returns a structured error (e.g. wip_limit_exceeded) rather than an exception. Agents identify people by email and labels by name; an unresolvable email or label name returns a structured validation_error (#512).
  • MCP clients can now fetch a full board snapshot (board://{board_id}) or a card's detail plus complete audit history (card://{card_id}) in a single read instead of chaining multiple tool calls, and the /mcp endpoint now sends CORS headers so browser-based MCP clients can connect (#513)
  • Maintenance mode — site admins can now put the instance into read-only mode from Admin → Settings, for upgrades and migrations. While it is active, every non-admin write is rejected with 503 Service Unavailable and a maintenance_mode error code, reads keep working, and all users see a configurable notice. Site admins are exempt and keep full read/write access. The setting is stored in the database, so it survives a restart, and takes effect immediately without one. Disabled by default — an existing install is unaffected until an operator turns it on.
  • Added an optional Show at-limit WIP indicator board setting (Board Settings → Rules → Limit enforcement, admin-only, off by default). When enabled, a column at exactly its WIP limit shows a calm WIP n/n indicator in place of the card count, instead of no ambient signal beyond the existing over-limit warning.
  • Added a personal card-density override: any board member can flip Use my own density in Board Settings → Display and pick comfortable/standard/dense for their own view, overriding the board's admin-set default without changing it for anyone else (#974)
  • CI gained a gitleaks-scan job that scans the full working tree for hardcoded secrets
  • on every MR and on main, backed by a documented .gitleaks.toml allowlist. It's also
  • wired as a local pre-commit hook (scripts/setup-hooks.sh) so a secret is caught before
  • it's even committed.
  • Added a compose-hygiene CI job running two new gates over the shipped Compose files: check-compose-image-pins.sh (every third-party image carries an explicit tag; first-party ${APP_VERSION} references are deliberately out of scope) and check-compose-project-names.sh (every standalone Compose file pins a distinct project name, compared on the default inside ${VAR:-…}, and overlays declare none). Both ship a --self-test mode that CI runs before the real invocation, per the house rule in #1093.
  • Issue Board Lens (experimental) — connect a public GitHub or GitLab repository to a board and view its issues as a read-only Visiban board, pivoting columns and swimlanes by status, milestone, label, or assignee (default: milestone swimlanes). Off by default; operators enable it with GIT_LENS_ENABLED=true.
  • The issue board lens gained a filter row — narrow by state (open/closed), milestone, and text (title or #number). State and milestone are applied server-side, so scoping to a milestone surfaces its issues even when they fall outside the lens's fetch budget (e.g. an older milestone in a large repo); text search runs client-side over the fetched set. Filters are link-shareable via the URL.
  • The experimental issue board lens gained a pipeline column view that derives a Backlog → To Do → Doing → Review → Done workflow from repository state: an issue moves to Doing when a feature branch for it exists, to Review when an open merge/pull request references or closes it, and to Done when it's closed. Each card shows the branch name or MR that placed it there. Branches and MRs are only fetched for the pipeline view (GitLab anonymous, gitlab.com public projects), bounded by the lens's shared cache.
  • The issue board lens now offers a Pipeline (workflow) column view in the toolbar and setup modal, rendering issues across Backlog → To Do → Doing → Review → Done. Each card shows why it landed where it did — the linked branch (Doing) and the open merge request that references or closes it (Review) — with the MR opening in a new tab.
  • The issue board lens gained native-board view comforts: collapse individual swimlanes or focus a single lane (both shareable via the URL), and a compact card-density toggle that strips cards to the essentials for an at-a-glance scan (persisted per user).

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Replaced Redis with Valkey — the BSD-3, Linux Foundation fork of Redis — as the Channels (WebSocket) and cache backend across Docker Compose (dev and production), CI, and the Helm chart (in-cluster service <release>-valkey-primary). Valkey is wire-compatible with Redis 7, so the redis:// URL scheme and the REDIS_URL, REDIS_CACHE_URL, REDIS_PASSWORD, and REDIS_PORT environment variables are unchanged. The store holds only ephemeral channel-layer and cache data, so no data migration is required — see the upgrade guide.
  • Bumped whitenoise 6.8.2 -> 6.12.0 (fixes a Range-request bug that could surface DB-connection errors in adjacent requests) and drf-nested-routers 0.94.1 -> 0.95.0 (maintenance release). Removed the dead @tootallnate/once entry from frontend/package.json overrides — no package in the dependency tree pulls it in.
  • The board now opens on the Lens tab when a lens is configured, and the Board tab is muted (never disabled or hidden) while the board has no native swimlanes (#1063).
  • Operator-visible change: docker-compose.prod.yml no longer defaults APP_VERSION to
  • the mutable latest tag. backend-init, backend, scheduler and frontend-build now
  • fail closed (docker compose pull/up -d and init-prod.sh exit immediately with a clear
  • message) if APP_VERSION is unset in .env. Any install whose .env already sets
  • APP_VERSION — the documented path since .env.example has always shipped a pinned value —
  • is unaffected. If your .env omits it, add APP_VERSION=v<version> before upgrading; see
  • docs/administration/upgrade.md ("Upgrading to 1.2.x").
  • Also added a scheduled CI job (check-release-images, ported from TruePPM) that fails if the
  • newest released backend/frontend image tag is missing from the GitLab registry or GHCR,
  • and documented both registries' retention/cleanup settings plus the digest-pinning option for
  • operators in the new docs/administration/container-image-retention.md (#1074).
  • Indexes and constraints are now built without locking the table. Every index Visiban adds from 1.2 onward uses CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY, and every check constraint is added NOT VALID and validated separately, so migrate no longer takes an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock on cards — previously a full read/write outage for the duration of an index build, and the blocker to documenting a zero-downtime upgrade. New visiban.db_operations wrappers provide the pattern (falling back to plain operations on SQLite installs), and a new manage.py check_migration_concurrency check runs in CI and fails on any migration that regresses to a blocking build via AddIndex, AddConstraint, db_index=True, unique=True, AlterUniqueTogether, or raw CREATE INDEX. The pattern and the decision to leave the fourteen pre-1.2 migrations untouched — with a documented build-by-hand procedure for operators replaying them against a populated database — are in the new Database migrations guide (#1081).
  • Card create, update, move, archive, unarchive and delete invariants now live in a
  • boards.services.cards service layer instead of inline in the REST views, so a
  • non-HTTP caller reaches the same WIP, weight, ownership, concurrency and audit-trail
  • enforcement. The REST and WebSocket contracts are unchanged. boards.permissions
  • gains get_board_roles(), a bulk role resolver that shares one precedence ladder
  • with get_board_role(), replacing a duplicate copy of those rules in the MCP tools.
  • Board templates now have a single source of truth: GET /api/v1/boards/templates/ and board creation both read the same BoardTemplate table, so a template can no longer be listed with different columns than it actually creates. Sending an unknown, explicit template slug to POST /api/v1/boards/ or POST /api/v1/groups/{id}/boards/ now returns 400 ({"code": ["unknown_template"], ...}) instead of silently creating a simple_kanban board — omitting template still defaults to simple_kanban as before. Two templates' column lists (project_delivery, legal_compliance) and every template's "done" column marking were corrected to match what board creation has actually been producing. Installed packages can now register additional templates via boards.hooks.TEMPLATE_PROVIDERS.
  • Helm chart values are now schema-validated, and unknown keys are rejected.
  • helm/visiban/values.schema.json declares additionalProperties: false on the
  • chart's own blocks, so a misspelled or invented values key now fails
  • helm install / helm upgrade with a message naming it, instead of being
  • accepted and silently changing nothing on the pod. Blocks passed through to a
  • subchart or to toYaml — global, postgresql, valkey,
  • ingress.annotations, *.resources — remain open.
  • If an existing values file carries a key the chart never read, that upgrade will
  • now fail. That is the intended behavior: the setting was not being applied
  • before either. Remove the key, or correct its spelling.
  • The ingress proxy-body-size annotation and the frontend nginx
  • client_max_body_size are now derived from the new
  • backend.settings.maxUploadSizeBytes (default 10 MB, +10 MB of framing
  • headroom), rather than being separate literals that could drift below the
  • application's own upload cap. Both resolve to the same values as before at the
  • chart defaults, so no existing install changes behavior. (The Trello import,
  • backend-schema-fuzz (added non-blocking in #1080) is now a blocking CI check (#1120). Its baseline findings were triaged: version-prefix fuzzing noise was fixed by excluding the internal UnsupportedVersionView catch-all from the OpenAPI schema, real board/card/column/swimlane/label ids are now seeded into path-parameter fuzzing via a schemathesis hook (backend/schemathesis_hooks.py) so the job exercises real endpoint logic instead of mostly 404s, and admin-only 403s are accepted as documented residual scope. A handful of already-tracked schema-accuracy gaps (#1119, #1123, #1124) are recorded as scoped, justified entries in backend/schemathesis-baseline.json rather than blocking this flip.
  • seed_demo_data now also creates a demo Group (owning the demo board), one CustomFieldDefinition with a value on a card, one SavedFilter, one CardAttachment, one GroupInviteLink, and one GroupLabel, and backend/schemathesis_hooks.py (#1120) maps their path parameters (group_pk/id under /api/v1/groups/, custom-fields/{id}, saved-filters/{filter_pk}, attachments/{attachment_pk}, invite-links/{link_id}, labels/{label_id} under groups) so the backend-schema-fuzz CI job can reach these resource families' real 200-path logic instead of always 404ing. Demo/test data only — no production behavior change (#1125).
  • Helm: the bundled Valkey now runs as the chart's own StatefulSet on the official, pinned valkey/valkey:8-alpine image (the same major as docker-compose.prod.yml) instead of the Bitnami valkey subchart, whose default image was the floating bitnami/valkey:latest. That tag meant a Helm install could switch Valkey major on any pod reschedule with no diff (it was Valkey 9 while Compose ran 8). The pod runs as a non-root user with a read-only root filesystem and no capabilities. The <release>-valkey-primary Service name and the backend's REDIS_URL / REDIS_CACHE_URL are unchanged. helm upgrade replaces the Valkey pod, which holds only rebuildable real-time and cache data, and fails with an explanation if the values still set valkey.architecture=replication, valkey.auth.enabled=true, or a Bitnami image. scripts/helm-structure-check.sh now fails any rendered image that is untagged or tagged latest. Chart version 0.5.0. See the upgrade guide.
  • Group detail routes (/api/v1/groups/<id>/...) now only match numeric ids, so no URL segment under /groups/ can be misrouted to a group action.
  • 17 CI jobs — migration-check, backend-schema-validate, backend-schema-fuzz, oidc-smoke, helm-lint, helm-template, backend-lint, broadcast-deferral, compose-hygiene, dockerfile-lint, frontend-lint, gate-selftest-parity, playwright-e2e, rbac-coverage, serializer-ts-parity, shellcheck, and ws-event-reachability — no longer run unconditionally on every merge to main. Each now runs only when a merge's own diff touches the paths its changes: rule already scopes on the MR pipeline. A docs-only merge previously still paid for a full DB migration cycle, OpenAPI schema validation, up to 600s of schemathesis fuzzing, a Keycloak boot, a full Helm chart lint/template/kubeconform pass, and a Playwright browser install, none of which could have been affected. Jobs that gate the image-publish path (backend-test, backend-test-coverage, frontend-test, and friends) are unchanged; so is trivy-scan, whose unconditional main run also catches CVEs newly disclosed against an unchanged pinned dependency (#1266).
  • Helm: backend.email.backend now defaults to "" (unset) instead of "smtp". Setting EMAIL_BACKEND pins the mail backend and disables the new Admin → Settings → Email UI, so the chart no longer emits it unless you configure it explicitly. The chart's render-time check for a placeholder fromAddress now fires only when backend.email.host is set, so you can install first and configure email from the admin UI afterwards. Set backend.email.backend explicitly to keep env-only behavior. Also adds backend.email.useSsl.
  • Staleness notifications now have their own Card has gone stale preference instead of being gated on Due date approaching, which described a different event entirely and is now wired to the due-date warning it is named after. Your existing setting is copied across on upgrade, so what you receive today does not change. Notification creation also now fires a post_notification_created signal — a stable extension point that lets additional delivery backends be added without modifying any file in the OSS core (#356). One consequence worth knowing: because Due date approaching now drives the due-date warning, anyone who had it on — which until now only opted them into staleness alerts — will start receiving the 24-hour due-date notification as well. Turn it off if you only wanted staleness; Card has gone stale keeps those coming either way.
  • The board's manual filter row now stays collapsed until it's used. The four always-visible Assignee, Label, Priority, and Due date dropdown buttons are replaced by a single + Filter menu (with an active-count badge) — picking a facet from it reveals that facet's own dropdown inline, which collapses again once closed. An active filter still renders as a removable chip below the filter bar, unchanged from before. Saved-filter tabs and the issue board lens's own filter row are unaffected (#964).
  • The dep-scan-osv CI job now runs on every MR and on main (previously gated to
  • lockfile changes plus a weekly schedule), and gates on advisory severity instead of a
  • blanket non-blocking allow_failure: true — HIGH/CRITICAL findings now block the
  • pipeline, MEDIUM/LOW/unscored findings warn without blocking.
  • The issue board lens now shares the board's toolbar row instead of rendering its own — the pivot dropdowns, a board-style Filters toggle, and the card-layout toggle sit on the same Row 2 as the view tabs, so switching between the Board and Lens tabs no longer shifts the layout. "Compact" card layout now matches the board too: cards flow two-per-row rather than just shrinking. The lens reuses the board's per-user card-layout preference.
  • A newly configured issue board lens now defaults to the Pipeline column view (Backlog → To Do → Doing → Review → Done) instead of Status — the pipeline is the opinionated, most useful view, whereas Status degrades to open/closed for repos without status:: labels. Existing lenses keep whatever view they were saved with.
  • The experimental issue board lens now caches each repository's rendered board once and shares it across all board members (GitLab) instead of fetching per viewer, serving results stale-while-revalidate behind a single-flight lock so many members viewing the same board no longer multiply outbound GitHub/GitLab API calls. Responses now support conditional requests (ETag/304). GitHub reads stay scoped to each viewer's own token.
  • The issue board lens toolbar now folds like the board's on narrow screens: below the large breakpoint the card-layout toggle moves into a Lens actions menu instead of pushing the row into a sideways scroll. The lens also picks up the same keyboard shortcuts as the board — F toggles the filter row and ⌘⇧L (Ctrl+Shift+L) switches card layout — so controls that look identical now behave identically.

Fixed
docs.text:
• Fixed real-time board updates silently stopping on connections idle for more than 5 seconds. backend/requirements.txt left the redis-py client unpinned, so fresh installs pulled redis-py 8.0.0, which enforces a 5-second socket read timeout on the block-forever BZPOPMIN that channels-redis uses in its receive loop — killing every idle WebSocket. redis-py is now pinned to >=4.6,<6.
  • Restored linux/arm64 container image publishing on release tags, alongside linux/amd64. :<tag>, :latest, and (for stable releases) the :MAJOR.MINOR alias are multi-arch manifest lists on both the GitLab registry and GHCR again. arm64 publishing had regressed silently since 2026-06-26 and was dropped from the release pipeline entirely when the amd64 push jobs moved to kaniko (#1084). If the arm64 build ever fails on a release tag, the amd64-only image is never published under the real tag names — the pipeline fails loudly instead of silently shipping a single-arch image under a multi-arch tag. The on-demand manual GHCR push jobs, which had no such safeguard, were removed.
  • Fixed the issue lens board 500ing when a provider sends non-string milestone_due/milestone_state metadata (int, dict, or unexpected shape). These fields are now coerced to None at the GitHub/GitLab normalization boundary, and the lens board view degrades to the last cached copy on any remaining unexpected parse error instead of failing with an internal server error (#1085).
  • Fixed the OpenAPI schema (/api/schema/) misdescribing the move, comments, checklist, column/swimlane reorder, share, and members custom actions — these previously fell back to the viewset's default serializer and documented the wrong request/response shape (e.g. move appeared to accept/return a full Card object instead of its real {column_id, swimlane_id, position, version} request and {card, movement} response, including its version_conflict / WIP / weight-limit error bodies). Also fixed related nullable-field gaps in CardSerializer and CardMovementSerializer (assignee, moved_by, last_moved_at, and several SerializerMethodFields) that a schema-vs-response contract test for move surfaced. A client generated from the schema (e.g. the MCP REST-client package, or any other external consumer) now gets accurate types for these endpoints.
  • Helm: a fresh helm install with the chart's default values now succeeds. Database migrations moved out of a pre-install/pre-upgrade hook Job and into a migrate init container on the backend Deployment. Helm runs pre-install hooks before it creates any release resource, so on a fresh install the hook tried to reach the bundled PostgreSQL before its StatefulSet and Service existed and the install never returned; helm upgrade was unaffected, which is why this survived. Concurrent backend replicas are serialized by a session-scoped PostgreSQL advisory lock (manage.py migrate_with_lock), so backendReplicaCount > 1 remains safe, and a replica that loses the race waits rather than starting against a half-migrated schema. The hook-managed bootstrap Secret is gone with the Job; a checksum/secret annotation on the backend pod template now carries secret.djangoSecretKey rotations into the same helm upgrade. Because the chart no longer declares any install hook, helm uninstall removes everything it created. New tunables: backend.migrate.connectTimeout and backend.migrate.lockTimeout.
  • Fixed the OpenAPI schema (/api/schema/) misdescribing five Group/GroupDetail fields: subgroup_count, board_count, and member_count were documented as string but are actually integer; is_starred was documented as string but is actually boolean; parent_name was documented as a non-nullable string but is null for a root group. Also fixed GroupDetail.ancestors, documented as string but actually an array of {id, name} objects. Schema-only change — no runtime behavior or response body change. A client generated from the schema now gets accurate types for these fields (#1119).
  • Fixed two more unhandled 500s and a schema-accuracy gap the now-blocking backend-schema-fuzz job (#1120) caught on its first real CI run:
  • POST/PATCH /api/v1/groups/{id}/labels/... crashed with an uncaught IntegrityError on a duplicate label name within the same group — the (group, name) uniqueness constraint isn't visible to DRF's automatic validator because group is injected after validation rather than being a serializer field. Now returns a clean 400.
  • POST /api/v1/groups/{id}/star/ documented the full Group response shape but actually returns a lean {"starred": bool} (by design, to avoid re-serializing the whole group) — the OpenAPI schema now matches.
  • GET /api/v1/cards/?updated_since= crashed with an uncaught DataError on PostgreSQL when the timestamp carried a UTC offset of 16 hours or more (valid ISO 8601, but out of range for timestamptz). Now returns a clean 400.
  • avatar_url (on BoardUser, CurrentUser, and the user-search response) was documented as format: uri, which a blank avatar (a valid, common value) fails — corrected to a plain string field, since fixing the underlying schema was less fragile than baselining every endpoint that happens to embed a user.
  • PATCH /api/v1/auth/user/ accepted a username containing an astral-plane Unicode code point (outside the Basic Multilingual Plane) — Django's own UnicodeUsernameValidator allows it, but it violates the documented username schema pattern for every consumer that (like JSON Schema and JavaScript) treats the response as UTF-16, breaking every subsequent response embedding that user for the rest of the run. Added a shared, stricter UsernameFormatValidator (accounts/validators.py) and applied it everywhere a username is written — self-profile update, registration, admin-created accounts, and choose-username — rather than baselining the resulting cascade of schema-conformance failures one endpoint at a time.
  • Fixed several unhandled 500s the backend-schema-fuzz CI job's baseline triage (#1120) turned up:
  • A non-numeric id in a request (board id, group id, board/group member user id, group invite-link id, group label id, or — defense in depth alongside a related routing-level fix — card/comment/attachment/checklist-item id) crashed instead of returning the documented 404. boards/views/_helpers.py and six other view modules resolved these with django.shortcuts.get_object_or_404, which doesn't catch the ORM's ValueError on an invalid pk the way rest_framework.generics's version does.
  • A malformed nested board-resource id (board/card/column/swimlane/label/custom-field) that no longer matches any URL pattern (a related, independent fix constraining those routes to digits landed on main just ahead of this branch) now gets a plain JSON 404 from a new catch-all route instead of Django's raw, unmatched-URL response — see the backend-schema-fuzz job comment in .gitlab-ci.yml for the full mechanism.
  • POST /api/v1/boards/{board_pk}/cards/{id}/move/ and POST /api/v1/groups/{id}/transfer-ownership/ crashed on a JSON request body that isn't an object (a bare number, string, array, null, or bool) — every request.data.get(...) call raised AttributeError on a non-mapping body. Both now return 400. (Other endpoints follow the same request.data.get(...)-without-a-type-check pattern and may still be exposed to the same crash if a future fuzz run's randomness happens to hit one — see the backend-schema-fuzz job comment in .gitlab-ci.yml.)
  • GET /api/v1/cards/ and GET /api/v1/boards/{board_pk}/cards/ crashed with an OverflowError when a board/column/swimlane/assignee/label filter value was outside the 64-bit integer range (e.g. ?column=1.03e34) — django_filters.NumberFilter's default bound (1e50) is far looser than what the database driver can actually bind. A new BoundedIdFilter (boards/views/_helpers.py) bounds these to the 64-bit range every id-backed model actually uses; out-of-range values now return 400.
  • Fixed PATCH /api/v1/boards/{board_pk}/custom-fields/{id}/ silently allowing a board admin to change a custom field's field_type (e.g. text -> number) after cards already hold values in it. Nothing revalidated, migrated, or cast the existing CustomFieldValue rows against the new type, so the change corrupted stale data in place — later readers (export, filtering, the upcoming Phase 2 card-face rendering) would trust field_type and crash or silently misrender against the old free-text/number/etc. content. field_type is now frozen once at least one value exists for the field; attempting to change it returns 400 naming the field instead of succeeding. A field with zero values is unaffected. Behavior change: a PATCH that previously succeeded (silently corrupting data) now returns 400 in this one case. There is intentionally no text -> dropdown (or other) conversion path in this release — deleting and recreating the field is the only way to change its type once it has values.
  • Fixed the OpenAPI schema (/api/schema/) misdescribing several Board/BoardFull fields: group_name is now documented as nullable, BoardFull.is_starred as a boolean, and BoardFull.group_detail as a nullable group summary, matching what the API actually returns. Schema-only change — no response bodies changed. A client generated from the schema now gets accurate types for these fields (#1123).
  • Fixed MoveBlockedToast not distinguishing an instance-wide maintenance-mode block from a personal permission error. A card move blocked by maintenance mode now leads with a fixed "The instance is temporarily read-only" sentence ahead of the operator's custom message, instead of the same generic "Move blocked" title used for other hard blocks — so it reads as a temporary, systemic condition rather than something wrong with the user's own access.
  • Declare every Issue Board Lens board query parameter (column_dim, swimlane_dim, state, milestone, labels, assignee, refresh) in the OpenAPI schema so API clients and schema tooling can see them. No runtime behavior change.
  • Custom field create, update, delete, and reorder events are now written to the board change feed, so clients replaying GET /api/v1/boards/<id>/events/?after= see schema changes they missed while disconnected.
  • Fixed the OpenAPI schema (/api/schema/) misdescribing eight fields as string (or, for one, with no type at all): Board.member_count and Board.card_count (actually integer), Board.is_starred (actually boolean), Board.group_detail (actually a nested GroupBrief object or null, now a real schema component), Board.allowed_priorities (actually an array of priority values), and CurrentUser.has_usable_password, uploads_enabled, and git_lens_enabled (all actually boolean). Schema-only change — no runtime behavior or response body change. A client generated from the schema now gets accurate types for these fields.
  • Fixed the OpenAPI schema declaring CurrentUser.email as format: email unconditionally, even though a blank email is a legitimate value (e.g. an account with no email on file). A strictly-conformant client would reject the API's own valid responses for such an account. email is still format-checked on write for non-blank values.
  • Fixed PATCH /api/v1/boards/{id}/ returning an unhandled 500 instead of a 400 when allowed_priorities was sent as a non-list JSON value (e.g. a bare boolean).
  • PATCH /api/v1/groups/<id>/board-defaults/ returned an unhandled 500 instead of a 400 when the request body was valid JSON but not a JSON object (a bare number, string, array, null or bool). It now returns 400 {"detail": "Request body must be a JSON object."}, matching the guard already applied to card move, group ownership transfer, and saved-filter creation.
  • Fixed the OpenAPI schema for GET /api/v1/boards/{id}/full/. It was documented as the plain Board shape, so its members rows, which can carry id: null (group-inherited members, the board owner, site admins) and role: "site_admin", did not match any published schema. /full/ is now documented as its own BoardFull component, and its members items as a new EffectiveBoardMember component that allows both. The response body is unchanged, and the strict BoardMembership component returned by POST /boards/{id}/members/ is unchanged too. Every existing component and enum name is preserved, and the only additions are BoardFull, EffectiveBoardMember and EffectiveBoardRoleEnum.
  • Fixed the OpenAPI schema (/api/schema/) understating nullability on Card.created_by, which is documented as always a BoardUser object even though the underlying FK is SET_NULL and returns null once the creating user is deleted. CardSerializer.created_by now declares allow_null=True so the published schema matches the real response shape. A client generated from the schema no longer needs to guard against an undocumented null.
  • Fixed nine places where the OpenAPI schema (/api/schema/) misdescribed a response field, all found by widening the serializer-ts-parity CI check from 5 component/interface pairs to 18 — every pair that has a schema component (#1139). CardComment.author, CardChecklistItem.created_by and GroupBrief.parent_name were published as non-nullable although each can legitimately be null (a deleted author, a pre-migration checklist row, a root group); GroupBrief.ancestors was published as string instead of a list of {id, name}; and CustomFieldDefinition.choices, SwimlaneCustomFieldDefinition.choices and Group.allowed_priorities were published with no type at all, so a generated client saw unknown/any where the first two are a list of strings and the third a list of priority slugs. All seven are documentation fixes: the runtime responses are unchanged, and request validation and its 400 error bodies are untouched. The frontend's CardMovement interface is also corrected — from_column_name, to_column_name, from_swimlane_name and to_swimlane_name are string, never null, because the underlying columns are NOT NULL with a "" default.
  • Corrected the OpenAPI schema for the column, swimlane, and custom-field reorder endpoints: they now document the bare array they actually return instead of a paginated {count, results} envelope. Schema-only; the response body is unchanged.
  • Fixed the "Also send by email" notification switch being unreachable by keyboard when its parent notification is off. Toggle previously used the native disabled attribute for this state, which removes a control from the tab order — the reason it's off was announced only in screen-reader browse mode. Toggle now supports an opt-in ariaDisabled prop: the switch stays focusable, click and keyboard (Space/Enter) activation are both ignored, and the same disabled visual styling is kept. The email notification switches now use it; plain disabled is unchanged everywhere else (#1159).
  • Fixed the Lens toolbar's Columns and Swimlanes pivot dropdown menus being clipped by the Row 2 toolbar strip's overflow-x-auto. Both now render their menus in a portal, matching the board's Overlay picker (#1147).
  • POST/PUT/PATCH /api/v1/groups/ now return 400 instead of 500 when allowed_priorities is not a list of strings, and the OpenAPI schema documents the 400 validation-error response on every operation that reads a request body or query parameters.
  • Fixed five endpoints returning a 500 instead of a 400 on invalid input: creating or renaming a column/label to a name already used on the board, moving a column to a position another column already occupies, sending a non-integer id to the column/swimlane reorder endpoints, and posting a non-object body to the board share endpoint. Also fixed group_name silently disappearing from PATCH /boards/{id}/ responses for an ungrouped board, and the OpenAPI schema for GET /boards/{id}/export-history/ describing the wrong response shape.
  • Fixed the OpenAPI schema understating nullability of assignee and created_by on the cross-board card query endpoint (GET /api/v1/cards/). Both are nullable foreign keys on Card — an unassigned card, or one whose creator was since deleted, has always returned null for these fields — but CardQuerySerializer declared them without allow_null=True, so the published schema described them as always present objects.
  • Fixed a bug where a non-admin member promoted to moderator could not see their own is_moderator status on GET /api/v1/boards/{id}/full/, hiding moderator-only controls (edit/delete others' content) from themselves in the UI.
  • Fixed the installation guide, .env.example, and scripts/release.sh to pin APP_VERSION to the actual published GHCR image tag form (v1.1.0) instead of a bare 1.1.0 tag that was never published, and normalized GET /api/v1/version/ to serve bare semver whenever APP_VERSION is pinned to a release tag, so the version API's documented contract holds — note this changes the value the endpoint returns for existing v-pinned installs, from the v-prefixed tag to bare semver (#1174).
  • allauth's per-IP rate limits (the failed-login lockout on the /accounts/ forms, signup and password reset) now key on the same client address as the API throttles instead of the reverse proxy's address, so one client can no longer exhaust them for everyone behind the bundled nginx (#1180).
  • Creating a card or swimlane custom field with a NUL byte in the name, help text, or a dropdown choice now returns a proper validation error instead of an unhandled server error (#1184)
  • Fixed PATCH/POST on /api/v1/boards/{id}/ and POST /api/v1/boards/import/ returning an unhandled 500 instead of a 400 (or a graceful fallback, for board import) when allowed_priorities, or a card's priority/movement_type/event_type/column/swimlane, contained a non-string item such as a nested list or object.
  • Fixed GroupViewSet.boards() copying a group's allowed_priorities onto every newly created board via a raw model save, which bypassed BoardSerializer validation and could propagate an unbounded, undeduped, or invalid-slug list from a group row saved before #1169's validator existed. The copy is now sanitized (capped, deduplicated, invalid entries dropped) before it is written to the new board.
  • Reject a NUL (0x00) byte in a text custom field value with a 400 instead of a 500, on both the card and swimlane write paths.
  • Converted BoardFullSerializer.group_name from a dotted-source CharField(source="group.name", default=None) to a SerializerMethodField, matching BoardSerializer.group_name's #1166 fix. BoardFullSerializer is only ever instantiated read-only today (/api/v1/boards/{id}/full/), so this had no live effect, but the dotted-source form silently drops the field from the response whenever the serializer is bound with partial=True and the board has no group — this closes that trap before any future reuse can reintroduce it. Schema (string, nullable, readOnly) and the /full/ response body are unchanged.
  • Fixed the member.added / member.updated WebSocket broadcast and the board change feed (GET /api/v1/boards/{id}/events/) hiding is_moderator on a non-admin member's own row. Both surfaces now apply the same self-row exception /full/ already had (#1173): a non-admin subscriber or reader sees is_moderator on the row that is their own membership, while every other member's row stays hidden.
  • Fixed BoardExportLogSerializer.actor not declaring allow_null=True, which caused the published OpenAPI schema to describe the export-history endpoint's actor field as always present, when BoardExportLog.actor is a nullable (SET_NULL) foreign key that is null for a deleted actor.
  • Also declared allow_null=True on four further nested serializer fields over the same kind of nullable foreign key — CardActivitySerializer.actor, CardAttachmentSerializer.uploaded_by, PublicCardSerializer.assignee, and NotificationSerializer.actor — for correctness and consistency with the rest of the schema. These four endpoints do not currently publish a named schema component for their response shape at all (a separate, pre-existing gap), so this part of the fix has no visible effect on the published document today, but corrects the field declaration ahead of that gap being closed. All five fields are read-only; the live API response was already null in each case.
  • Hosted demo: deleting a comment or an attachment, adding a card relation, starring a board, and "Mark all read" on notifications are now refused up front with an aria-disabled affordance and the shared "This is a shared demo — …" copy, instead of falling through to the generic DemoWriteBlockedToast. The theme-preference sync — a background save the visitor never clicked — is now silently skipped in demo mode rather than shown as a refusal (#1193).
  • Fixed an intermittent failure in the rich-text editor's bold-toolbar end-to-end test, which could click the toolbar before the editor had registered the keyboard selection. The editor itself was not affected.
  • The scheduled check-release-images job now fails when a release tag resolves but its manifest does not cover both linux/amd64 and linux/arm64, and the arm64 release pushes retry transient registry failures instead of failing the release on the first one.
  • Fixed CI jobs hitting Docker Hub's anonymous-pull rate limit (429 Too Many Requests), most visibly on the helm-install/helm-netpol drills' fresh, credential-less docker:dind daemon. Docker Hub image references in .gitlab-ci.yml now resolve through the GitLab Dependency Proxy, and the backend/frontend Dockerfiles take a BASE_REGISTRY build arg (default docker.io/library, so local and contributor builds are unaffected) that CI points at the proxy. Requires the Dependency Proxy to be enabled for the visiban GitLab group.
  • Fixed logging in with an email address. The login form has always said "Username or email", but only the username was ever accepted. The username field of POST /api/v1/auth/login/ (and the optional email field) now accepts either the username or the account's email address, matched case-insensitively. A username always takes precedence, and an email address shared by more than one account logs into none of them. Failed attempts by username and by email now count toward a single per-account lockout, so switching identifiers no longer doubles an attacker's guesses.
  • Fixed the OpenAPI schema (/api/schema/) misdescribing 4 endpoints that survived #1108's sweep: GET .../cards/{id}/activities/ and .../attachments/ previously fell back to the wrong component (Card) entirely, and GET /api/notifications/ and GET /api/share/{token}/ published no response body at all. All four now publish their real response shape, including correct nullability on CardActivity.actor, CardAttachment.uploaded_by, Notification.actor, Notification.card_title/board_name, and the public-share card's assignee. A client generated from the schema now gets accurate types for these endpoints. scripts/check-serializer-ts-parity.py now also checks these newly-published CardActivity, CardAttachment, Notification, and PublicCard schema components against their TypeScript interfaces.
  • Fixed a slowdown when opening large boards: GET /api/v1/boards/{id}/full/ loads noticeably faster on boards with thousands of cards. The card serializers now read attachments, checklist items, movements, and custom field values from prefetched lists instead of calling .all() on each card's related managers, which rebuilt a Django queryset per card per relation even though no extra SQL was issued. The response is unchanged (#1212).
  • Fixed nightly-load-test (#1082) never actually running — its required GitLab pipeline
  • schedule (CI/CD → Schedules, cron 0 3 * * *, LOAD_TEST_SCHEDULE=true) was never created,
  • so the real p95 latency budget it enforces was never checked, and a genuine ~40% regression
  • on GET /boards/{id}/full/ shipped undetected. The schedule now exists, and a new
  • schedule-config-check job runs on every scheduled pipeline to fail loudly if any
  • $CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "schedule" && $VAR == "true"-gated job in .gitlab-ci.yml ever loses
  • its GitLab-side schedule again — this class of gap left no trace in the repo before now.
  • backend/nightly-load-test-baseline.json stays "provisional" until the first real scheduled
  • run re-derives it (see docs/development/nightly-load-test.md).
  • Fixed parent_name silently disappearing from PATCH /api/v1/groups/{id}/ responses for top-level (root) groups. The field is now a SerializerMethodField, immune to DRF's unconditional SkipField on a partial=True-bound serializer.
  • Django admin static assets now load on Helm and Docker Compose production installs: the collectstatic init/setup step's output is shared with the running backend container via a volume, instead of being discarded in a container filesystem the backend never sees. Previously /admin/ could 500 with a missing staticfiles manifest error.
  • Fixed missing keyboard-focus indicators on role="menuitem" items in the bulk-action toolbar's Move/Assign/Priority menus, the board and lens Collapse/Expand split-button menus, and the board's overflow ("More board actions") menu. These menus already supported full roving-tabindex arrow-key navigation, but a keyboard user arrowing between items saw no visible indicator of which one was focused. All four now carry the same focus:ring-2 focus:ring-primary-emphasis ring as SingleSelectDropdown and UserMenu, sourced from a new shared MENU_ITEM_FOCUS_RING constant so the gap can't reappear at a fifth site.
  • Fixed scripts/release.sh silently failing to pin the Helm chart's default backend/frontend image tags to the release version — the sed anchored on 2-space indentation while helm/visiban/values.yaml's tag: lines are 4-space indented, so the chart's default tags had been stuck at v1.1.0 since before the 1.1.0 GA. The fix scopes the rewrite to only the tag: line immediately following a ghcr.io/visiban/visiban/backend or .../frontend repository line, so the bundled Valkey and helm test curl probe image tags at the same indentation are never touched.
  • A successful password change through POST /api/v1/auth/password/change/ now clears a pending administrator-forced password change (must_change_password), as POST /api/v1/auth/change-password/ always did. Previously a user who changed their password through this endpoint stayed blocked from every other endpoint. Both endpoints now share one post-change step that clears the flag and revokes Personal Access Tokens in the same transaction as the password save (#1259).
  • Fixed scripts/release.sh's own RC-banner consistency check never matching, so it always warned on a valid release candidate. The check looked for the substring rc.N is the current..., but the banner the script itself writes is **1.2.0-rc.1** is the current stable release candidate... — the bolded, full-version form. The check now matches what the script actually writes.
  • Removed a dead version-bump step in scripts/release.sh that tried to rewrite a hardcoded APP_VERSION: line in docker-compose.yml. That file no longer sets APP_VERSION (it builds the dev stack locally instead of pulling a tagged image), so the step's grep guard was always false and it never ran.
  • Fixed scripts/release.sh never updating docs/index.md's release banner for alpha/beta versions — only rc.N and stable releases were handled, so cutting an alpha or beta left docs.visiban.com showing the previous cycle's stale banner with no mention of the pre-release. Alpha/beta now get their own banner wording, and the banner-rewrite logic across all three stages now correctly recognizes and replaces each other's banner text, so a release can transition through any stage boundary (alpha → beta, beta → rc, or straight to GA) without leaving two banners in the file.
  • Password-reset emails now link to the configured frontend origin instead of http://localhost:5173. FRONTEND_URL was read into the login and logout redirect settings but never defined under its own name, so the reset-link builder's lookup always fell through to the development default — on every install that had set the variable (#356).
  • allowed_priorities on boards now rejects falsy non-list values (false, 0, "", {}) with a 400 instead of storing them and returning a payload that violates the documented array schema.
  • Fixed board-scoped API endpoints (boards, columns, swimlanes, labels, cards, custom field definitions, board members, comments, attachments, checklist items) returning a 500 instead of a 404 when a non-numeric id was passed in the URL. Discovered via the CI schema-fuzz job; the underlying models all use plain integer ids, so a garbage id now fails to match the route and 404s cleanly instead of reaching the database layer.
  • Pinned certbot/certbot to v5.8.0 in docker-compose.prod.yml. It was the only unpinned image in the production stack — postgres, valkey and nginx all carried floors — and it is the service that owns TLS issuance and renewal, so it floated to whatever latest pointed at on every docker compose pull, with no diff and no pipeline event. v5.8.0 is what latest resolved to at the time of the pin, so the change is a no-op today and a floor from here on.
  • Fixed the production Docker Compose install (init-prod.sh / docker-compose.prod.yml), which could not serve on a fresh install. nginx crash-looped on a malformed start command; the backend never turned healthy because its healthcheck sent Host: localhost, which an ALLOWED_HOSTS holding only the public domain rejects, so nginx never started (the healthcheck now sends Host: $DOMAIN); and the one-time admin password was written inside the exited backend-init container, so docker compose exec backend cat /tmp/visiban_admin_password never found it. Upgrade note: DOMAIN must now appear in ALLOWED_HOSTS, or the backend never turns healthy.
  • Fixed re-running init-prod.sh to switch TLS_MODE or pick up a regenerated certificate silently keeping the old nginx config, and nginx never loading certificates the certbot service renewed (it now reloads every 6 hours).
  • Fixed a database or Valkey password containing / (about half of all openssl rand -base64 outputs, which the docs recommended) breaking startup. The Helm chart now percent-encodes credentials in database-url; init-prod.sh rejects a Compose password containing / ? # % [ ] or whitespace up front; and the backend fails with a clear ImproperlyConfigured instead of an error or warning that printed part or all of the database or Valkey password to the log. The docs now generate these with openssl rand -hex 32. Upgrade note: if you percent-encoded externalDatabase.password by hand to work around this, give the plain value again — the chart now encodes it.
  • Fixed the upgrade docs for the production Compose stack: they rebuilt images the stack never builds and never changed APP_VERSION, so an "upgrade" kept running the old release. The procedure is now set APP_VERSION, pull, up -d.
  • The development and production Docker Compose stacks no longer resolve to the same Compose project. docker-compose.prod.yml pinned no name:, so it took the checkout directory — visiban on a default clone — which is what docker-compose.yml also defaulted to. Both files declare a bare pgdata: volume and both define db, valkey and backend, so the two stacks shared visiban_pgdata and could recreate each other's containers in place. Because Postgres applies POSTGRES_PASSWORD only on first init, whichever stack started second met the other's password — or the development SECRET_KEY landed on production data. Production is unaffected (visiban is what it already resolved to); the development stack now defaults to visiban-dev and starts a fresh database — see the upgrade note in the installation guide.
  • Fixed the scheduled main pipeline going red on dockerfile-lint. The job ran hadolint/hadolint:latest-alpine, which floated into hadolint 2.15 and introduced DL3066 (non-numeric user-id in USER) — turning a green job red with no Dockerfile change. The image tag is now pinned to v2.15.1-alpine, and DL3066 is ignored in .hadolint.yaml: both backend Dockerfiles create the runtime user with an explicit fixed uid (adduser --uid 1001), so USER visiban always resolves to 1001 inside the image.
  • Group invite-link join URLs (/api/v1/groups/join/<token>/) no longer get routed to a group action when the token matches an action name such as star or labels; they now always reach the join endpoint.
  • Fixed the issue board lens's single-flight fetch lock expiring mid-fetch on the Pipeline view. The lock is what stops several viewers all calling the provider at once, and it was sized for the issue pages alone (45s) while a Pipeline fetch also pages through branches and merge requests — up to 70s. Under a slow provider the lock could lapse while a fetch was still running and let a second viewer start another one. Now sized to the real worst case. This surfaces more often since new lenses default to the Pipeline view.
  • The Refresh button on an issue board lens now forces a re-fetch of the latest upstream issues (and updates the "Synced … ago" time), instead of being served the still-fresh cached copy within the cache's soft-TTL window.
  • scripts/release.sh no longer closes every remaining open issue in the milestone when the version being cut is a pre-release (-alpha.N, -beta.N, -rc.N). Previously the first alpha of a release would have marked all of that milestone's still-open GA blockers as done. The milestone is now closed only by the stable tag that ends it.
  • POST /api/v1/boards/{id}/saved-filters/ no longer crashes with a 500 error when sent a non-object JSON body (e.g. a top-level array); it now returns a 400 with a clear error message.
  • Fixed backend-schema-fuzz failing on main after #1121: PATCH/PUT /api/v1/boards/{board_pk}/custom-fields/{id}/ legitimately return 400 once field_type is frozen by an existing value, but that response wasn't in the accepted-failure baseline. Baselined alongside the other custom-fields write endpoints (#1124); no application behavior changed.
  • Fixed the OpenAPI schema for CurrentUser.username and BoardUser.username incorrectly declaring an ASCII-only pattern, even though the API has always accepted international usernames. Clients validating strictly against the published schema would reject legitimate non-ASCII usernames.
